content.user_title: Replace Flaky Test Delays With Condition Waiting
content.value_statement: Flaky tests fail when they depend on guessed delays instead of observable state. This skill helps Claude, Codex, and Claude Code replace sleeps with condition-based polling.
actual_capabilities: Explains when to replace setTimeout, sleep, and time.sleep in tests.
Provides a generic waitFor polling pattern with timeout handling.
Shows event, state, count, file, and compound condition waiting examples.
Includes TypeScript helpers for event type, event count, and predicate matching.
Defines cases where a documented arbitrary timeout remains valid.
Lists common mistakes such as fast polling, missing timeouts, and stale data.
limitations: Does not execute tests or modify files by itself.
Examples target TypeScript-style async tests and may need adaptation.
File existence polling should stay within trusted test paths.
Does not replace timing assertions for debounce or throttle behavior.

use_cases.title: Stabilize CI Tests
use_cases.description: Replace guessed sleeps in failing asynchronous tests with polling based on real events or state.

use_cases.title: Review Async Test Patterns

prompt_templates.title: Find Delay Replacements
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner review of one flaky test.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this flaky test and identify any setTimeout, sleep, or fixed delay that should become condition-based waiting.

prompt_templates.title: Convert One Test
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate rewrite of a known failing test.
prompt_templates.prompt: Rewrite this async test so it waits for the actual event, state change, or count instead of a guessed delay.

prompt_templates.title: Design Wait Helpers
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced helper design for a test suite.
prompt_templates.prompt: Design reusable condition-based wait helpers for this event stream, including timeout behavior and clear failure messages.

prompt_templates.title: Audit Test Strategy
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit this async test suite for race conditions, stale reads, unsafe polling intervals, and justified timing waits.

output_examples.input: A test sleeps for 300 ms before checking that two tool calls started.
output_examples.output: The skill recommends waiting until two matching tool-call events exist, then continuing the test.

output_examples.input: A polling helper checks cached state and has no timeout.
output: Move the state lookup inside the polling loop.
Add a clear timeout and failure message.

output_examples.input: A debounce test uses a fixed 200 ms delay.
output_examples.output: The skill keeps the delay only when the test documents the debounce interval and waits for the trigger first.

best_practices: Start each wait after the action that should trigger the condition.
Use explicit timeouts with failure messages that name the missing condition.
Poll at a modest interval and fetch fresh state inside each check.
anti_patterns: Replacing every delay without checking whether timing behavior is the subject.
Polling every millisecond or without a termination condition.
Waiting on broad conditions that can pass before the expected behavior occurs.

faq.question: Does this skill run tests?
faq.answer: No. It gives patterns and helper designs for improving tests you run in your own project.

faq.question: Can I use it outside TypeScript?
faq.answer: Yes. The core condition polling pattern applies to other languages with async test support.

faq.question: Should I remove every sleep from tests?
faq.answer: No. Keep timed waits when timing behavior is the thing being tested and document the reason.

faq.question: How should I choose a timeout?
faq.answer: Use a timeout that covers expected slow CI behavior and produces a clear failure message.

faq.question: Is file waiting safe?
faq.answer: Use file existence checks only for trusted test paths and avoid polling arbitrary user paths.

faq.question: Does it support Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The guidance supports Claude, Codex, and Claude Code workflows.
